aura:
aura — control AuraOS from the terminal

Usage: aura <command> [resource] [name...] [flags]
       aura <command> --help


Basics
  aura jump                                Pick a running app or service and shell into it
  aura jump <app|inst>                     Shell into an app sandbox
  aura jump <app> --sidecar <name>         Shell into a sidecar
  aura mount                               Pick apps to mount into a container, live (wizard)
  aura mount add <app...>                  Mount apps into this app (--wr writable, --instance <inst>)
  aura cap grant                           Pick the CLI tools an app may use
  aura dev new                             Start the create-new-app wizard
  aura ps                                  Running instances (= aura get inst)
  aura run <app>                           Start an app, print instance id
  aura status                              Health: shell, apps, capabilities, services
  aura info                                Execution context: layers, OS, env, mounts

Inspect
  aura get apps [name]                     Installed apps + instance count
  aura get inst [name]                     Running instances
  aura get inst <name> sidecars            Sidecars of one instance + their IDs
  aura get sidecars [name]                 All sidecars
  aura get act [name]                      Open windows of running instances
  aura get caps [name]                     Shareable CLI capabilities
  aura get svc [name]                      Services on the master (sshd, code-server …)
  aura get mounts [name]                   Cross-app mounts
  aura get ports [name]                    Port exposes (app-to-app or host)
  aura get scopes [name]                   Install scopes (system / global / user)
  aura get themes [name]                   Theme presets, ACTIVE marks the one in use
  aura get perms [app]                     Declared manifest permissions
  aura get iface [app/name]                Interface Registry: MCP, REST, WS … (URL: $OS_API_BASE + url)
  aura describe <resource> <name>          Full YAML of one resource (-o json)
  aura logs inst <name>                    Output of an instance (-f to follow)
  aura logs inst <name> -c <sidecar>       Logs of an instance sidecar
  aura logs svc <name>                     Logs of a service
  aura events                              Live stream of OS state changes
  Output for get: -o wide | json | yaml | name

Lifecycle
  aura start|stop|restart app <app...>     Start, stop or restart an app (all its instances)
  aura start|stop|restart inst <inst...>   Start (resume), stop or restart single instances
  aura start|stop|restart svc <svc...>     Start, stop or restart services
  aura pause inst <inst...>                Pause instances (onPause)
  aura resume inst <inst...>               Resume paused instances (onResume)
  aura kill inst <inst...>                 Force-kill (SIGKILL, no hooks)
  aura enable app <app...>                 Re-arm autoStart/warmPool, show in dock + launcher
  aura disable app <app...>                Stop all instances, hide from dock + launcher

Install & remove
  aura install app <dir>                   Install an app from a directory
  aura install cap [names...]              Install capabilities (picker if empty)
  aura install svc <name>                  Install a service
  aura install sdk                         Install the @aura/* SDK packages
  aura rm app <app...>                     Delete apps and all their data
  aura rm act <act...>                     Close windows
  aura rm svc <svc...>                     Uninstall services
  aura rm cap <cap...>                     Uninstall capabilities
  aura rm mount <mount...>                 Detach mounts (-i <inst> if several have it)
  aura rm port <port...>                   Remove port exposes (ids from aura get ports)
  aura rm sc <sidecar...>                  Delete OS-managed sidecars (inside their app)

Connect
  aura exec inst <name>                    Shell into an instance
  aura exec inst <name> -c <sidecar>       Shell into a sidecar
  aura exec inst <name> -- <cmd...>        Run a command
  aura open inst <name>                    Open a new window on an instance
  aura mount ...                           Mount another app's files, live
  aura port ...                            Expose a TCP port to an app or the host
  aura data ...                            Query / write / watch content providers

Access
  aura grant perms <app> [names...]        Grant permissions (picker if empty)
  aura grant caps <app> [names...]         Grant capabilities (picker if empty)
  aura revoke perms <app> <names...>       Revoke permissions
  aura revoke caps <app> <names...>        Revoke capabilities
  aura grant|revoke caps … --template <t>  Caps of a sidecar template (persistent)
  aura grant|revoke caps … --sidecar <n>   Caps of one running OS sidecar (inside its app)
  aura cap ...                             Manage the capability registry
  aura grant nperm <app> <locked|popup>    Grant Locked / pop-up notifications
  aura grant nperm <app> read --scope app:<id>|sender:<key>|all  Let an app read other senders' notifications (--include-secret)
  aura revoke nperm <app> <locked|popup|read>  Revoke them again, takes effect at once
  aura get nperm [app]                     Requested vs granted notification features
  aura admin ...                           grants · audit · access-report · contract-report · notif release
  aura runtime ...                         Runtimes apps run in: ls · show · default · set · enable|disable · override · migrate
  aura whoami                              Server-verified identity, and local hints
  aura setup-code                          Host: one-time owner setup code
  aura user reset-password <username>      Host: one-time password reset code
  aura admin user ...                      Host: member accounts (D82): add · ls · disable|enable · reset-password · grant|revoke use|jump
  aura system reidentify                   Host: new systemId and key for a copied /data
  aura approve <id>                        Host: approve (--deny) a pending owner approval as the operator
  aura secret ask <name>                   Ask the owner to type a secret for an app (--for <app>) in the desktop dialog
  aura apikey ...                          API keys for REST callers: create · ls · revoke
  Grants, API keys, the audit and manifest edits are the owner's: in the System Terminal they wait for your approval in the desktop (privileged ones with your password); on the host (docker exec -it aura-shell aura …) they run directly. There is no admin login.

Ecosystem & dev
  aura nexus ...                           Find, install, update, publish apps
  aura dev ...                             Scaffold, validate, run apps standalone; rebuild/restart AuraOS
  aura mode ...                            Developer Mode: show it, switch it (on asks for your password)
  aura release ...                         Normal Mode releases: status · ls · build · activate · rollback (Phase 6)

Settings
  aura set theme <name>                    Switch the active theme
  aura completion bash|zsh                 eval "$(aura completion bash)"
  aura api-resources                       All resource types, short names, verbs

Short names: app inst sc act cap svc mount port host iface scope theme perm nperm

Flags
  --shell-url <url>                        Default: $OS_API_BASE or http://127.0.0.1:3000
  -V, --version                            Print version
  -h, --help                               Show help

aura jump:
Usage: aura jump|j [options] [target]

Open a session inside a running app's real environment in this terminal (D74).
Your home there is --home private (default: your Private Home, as your user),
app (the app's App Home, as the app's identity) or ephemeral (an empty home,
gone on exit). Without a target: interactive picker. With a target (app id or
instance id): straight in; add --sidecar to enter one of its sidecars (owner
only, the image's user).

Options:
  -s, --sidecar <id>  Enter this sidecar of the target instead (IDs: aura get
                      inst <id> sidecars)
  --home <mode>       private (default) | app | ephemeral
  --no-services       Picker: hide services, show only user apps
  --no-apps           Picker: hide apps, show only services
  -m, --master        Skip the picker and jump straight into the aura-shell
                      master container
  -h, --help          display help for command

aura build:
Usage: aura build [options] <resource> [names...]

Build apps for production (`astro build`, in a throwaway container). An app
runs from its build while the build matches its sources, and with `astro dev`
again as soon as you edit it — so building never costs you hot editing. Running
instances switch on their next start, or now with --restart.

Options:
  --all       every enabled app whose sources changed since its last build (or
              that was never built)
  --force     build even when the build is current
  --restart   restart running instances onto the new build now (windows come
              back; Terminal and OpsConsole always switch on their next start)
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: aura mount [options] [command] [appId...]

Mount another app's files into this app's container, live and without a

Arguments:

                                  the interactive wizard

Options:
  --instance <id>                 Target instance (default: $APP_INSTANCE_ID)
  --wr                            Mount WRITE (default: read-only)
  --data                          Mount the target's data dir instead of its
                                  source
  --patches                       Mount the app's patch repository at
                                  /mnt/aura/patches/<appId> (writable; Track P)
  -h, --help                      display help for command

Commands:
  ls|list [options]               List what is currently mounted into an
                                  instance.
  add [options] [appId...]        Mount one or more apps into the target
                                  instance. With no appId, opens an interactive
                                  picker over every installed app
                                  (system/global/user — switch scope with m).
  workspace                       Developer Mode: mount the AuraOS source
                                  (/workspace) read-write at
                                  /mnt/aura/workspace of THIS System Terminal.
                                  The owner approves it with one click; it
                                  lasts until `aura mount rm workspace`, the
                                  Terminal stops, or Developer Mode is switched
                                  off.
  rm|remove [options] [appId...]  Detach mounts. A bare appId detaches all of
                                  its mounts (source, data, patches, work);
                                  pass `<appId>:data`, `<appId>:patches` or
                                  `<appId>:work` for just that one. With no
                                  args, opens a picker.

aura cap:
Usage: aura cap|capability [options] [command]

Manage shareable CLI capabilities (opt-in binaries bind-mounted into PRoot
apps).

Options:
  -h, --help                          display help for command

Commands:
  list|ls [options]                   List capabilities from the registry with
                                      install status and which apps declare
                                      them.
  install <name...>                   Install one or more capabilities from the
                                      registry into the shared toolchain (the
                                      owner approves each).
  update [options] [name...]          Re-pull installed capabilities from their
                                      source (npm/apt/curl) so the toolchain
                                      copy matches upstream. With no names,
                                      updates every installed non-builtin cap.
                                      Routes through the same shell endpoint as
                                      install, so running apps see the new
                                      binaries without a respawn.
  doctor [options] [name...]          Check that every installed capability can
                                      actually RUN in each sandbox — i.e. that
                                      its shared libraries travel with it. A
                                      cap that installs cleanly and dies at
                                      exec with "cannot open shared object
                                      file" looks healthy to every other
                                      command; this is what surfaces it.
  remove <name>                       Uninstall a capability + remove it from
                                      every app manifest that declares it.
  grant [options] [appId] [name...]   Grant capabilities to an app. With tool
                                      names: adds them (use '*' for all, '#'
                                      for all-except). With no names (or -i):
                                      opens an interactive picker to
                                      check/uncheck tools, showing what is
                                      already granted. Hot-refreshes running
                                      instances — no respawn.
  revoke [options] <appId> <name...>  Remove a capability from an app manifest
                                      and restart running instances.
  info <name>                         Print registry entry + install status +
                                      apps declaring this capability.
  registry                            Inspect the capability registry, or add
                                      your own capability definitions (the
                                      owner approves).
  help [command]                      display help for command
